facts.statement: The type specimen, a skull, atlas, and axis, was discovered in 2010 in the Romualdo Formation of the Araripe Basin in Brazil.
facts.quote: Maaradactylus is based on the Museu Paleontologico de Santana do Cariri specimen MPSC R 2357, a skull, atlas, and axis discovered in 2010 in the Aptian-Albianaged Romualdo Formation of Sítio São Gonçalo, Santana do Cariri, Ceará, in the Araripe Basin of Brazil.

facts.statement: The genus was described by Renan Bantim and colleagues in 2014.
facts.quote: Maaradactylus was described by Renan Bantim and colleagues in 2014.

facts.statement: The generic name honors Maara, a river monster from Cariri legends who devoured fishermen.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to Maara, in the legends of the Cariri the daughter of a chief, by sorcery changed into a river monster with long teeth, devouring fishermen.

facts.statement: The suffix 'dactylus' refers to the long fourth wing finger, derived from the Greek word for 'finger'.
facts.quote: The suffix ~dactylus is common in the names of pterosaurs and is derived from Greek δάκτυλος, daktylos, "finger", referring to the long (fourth) wing finger.

facts.statement: The species name honors Alexander Kellner, a leading Brazilian pterosaur expert.
facts.quote: The specific name honors Alexander Kellner, Brazil's foremost pterosaur expert.

facts.statement: In 2019, Megan L. Jacobs and colleagues reassigned the species formerly known as Coloborhynchus spielbergi to the genus Maaradactylus.
facts.quote: In 2019, the species Coloborhynchus spielbergi, also assigned as Anhanguera spielbergi, was reassigned to Maaradactylus by Megan L. Jacobs and colleagues as M. spielbergi.

facts.statement: Maaradactylus lived during the Aptian to Albian stages of the Lower Cretaceous in northeastern Brazil.
facts.quote: Maaradactylus is a genus of anhanguerid pterodactyloid pterosaur known from the Lower Cretaceous (Aptian to Albian) Romualdo Formation of northeastern Brazil.

facts.statement: The prominent crest on Maaradactylus was triangular in shape and approximately 9.2 cm tall.
facts.quote: The prominent crest was triangular in shape and around 9.2 cm tall in the only known specimen.

facts.statement: The nasoantorbital fenestra was approximately 40% of the skull's length and more than twice as long as it was tall.
facts.quote: The nasoantorbital fenestra was around 40% of the length of the skull over twice as long as tall.

facts.statement: Maaradactylus is classified within the family Anhangueridae.
facts.quote: Maaradactylus is recognized as belonging to the family Anhangueridae.

facts.statement: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis identified Maaradactylus as the closest relative of Anhanguera.
facts.quote: A 2019 phylogenetic analysis by Megan Jacobs and colleagues found Maaradactylus to be the sister taxon (closest relative) of Anhanguera.

facts.statement: Later studies found that the previously identified sister taxon, Cearadactylus, is a synonym of Brasileodactylus, making Brasileodactylus the closest relative of Maaradactylus.
facts.quote: However, these studies find Maaradactylus to be the sister taxon of Cearadactylus. Later work found "Cearadactylus" to be a junior synonym of Brasileodactylus, and a phylogenetic analysis incorporating this found the revised Brasileodactylus as the sister taxon of Maaradactylus.

facts.statement: The skull indicates a wingspan of nearly six meters and possesses 35 pairs of teeth in the upper jaw.
facts.quote: Este cráneo, uno de los mayores cráneos de anhanguéridos de la cuenca y que indica una envergadura de cerca de seis metros, tiene una cresta relativamente alta que corre a lo largo de la línea media del premaxilar, el cual compone la mayor parte de la región superior del pico, y posee 35 pares de dientes en el maxilar.

facts.statement: Maaradactylus lived between 119.57 and 113.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Aptian to Aptian (119.57 to 113.2 million years ago)
